Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back to the all-important run chase. The umpires are back out in the middle and the Indian players form a huddle before taking their places on the field. It will be the duo of Phoebe Litchfield and skipper Alyssa Healy to open the innings for Australia Women. The sun is going down and the weather is getting cooler. There might be some dew later on as well. Kashvee Gautam will take the new ball for India Women. Let's go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Looking ahead - With the deck showing signs of a turn and variable bounce, India Women will look for early wickets to defend this total and level the three-match series. The Aussies will need the batting unit to fire again and get past this Indian total to gain a 6-4 lead in this multi-format series. We will be back in a bit with the chase.

Skipper Kaur rallies the lower order - In the final phase, India’s captain Harmanpreet Kaur stood tall to steer the team out of trouble. Battling a lingering knee injury from the previous match, Kaur anchored the innings with a crucial half-century. She found valuable support from the lower order, including Kashvee Gautam and Kranti Gaud, who contributed vital runs to help push the total past the 250-run mark. For Australia, Annabel Sutherland, Ashleigh Gardner and Alana King bowled well and picked up two each, while Nicola Carey and Megan Schutt chipped in with one apiece.

Aussie spinners trigger a dramatic collapse - The second phase saw a sharp shift in momentum as Australia’s bowlers, led by their spinners, tightened the screws around the 18th over. After Smriti's dismissal, Jemimah Rodrigues walked in but failed to make an impact, departing for 11 after nicking a ball from Annabel Sutherland to the keeper. The biggest blow came when the well-set Pratika Rawal on 52 suffered a brainfade, resulting in a run-out that completely turned the tables in Australia's favour. Spinners Ashleigh Gardner and Alana King capitalized on the pressure, picking up two wickets each as the Indian middle order struggled with pace variations. Deepti Sharma fell cheaply for 1, and while Richa Ghosh and Amanjot Kaur got starts, they were unable to convert them into big scores.

Brilliant opening stand sets the platform - The first phase of the innings belonged entirely to India as the openers laid a solid foundation, scoring freely to put the Australian attack under pressure. Pratika Rawal and Smriti Mandhana looked comfortable early on, stitching together a 78-run opening partnership. While Mandhana was not at her fluent best, surviving a few edges and dropped chances, she provided the necessary support to the more compact Pratika. The breakthrough finally came when Ashleigh Gardner cleaned up Mandhana for 31 off 37 balls after she attempted a ramp.

India posts a competitive total - India Women posts a hard-fought total of 251 runs after 50 overs, setting a challenging target for Australia at the Bellerive Oval in Hobart. Despite a dramatic middle-order collapse, a captain’s knock from Harmanpreet Kaur ensured the visitors have a defendable score on a surface that looks like a good one for batting.

Oh, an overthrow and India Women do cross the crucial 250-run mark on the final ball. Good-length delivery, around off, Vaishnavi pushes it to extra cover and sets off for the single. The fielder has a shy at the bowler's end but misses and the batters manage to pick up the second run as the fielder backing up is a bit deep. India Women finish with 251/9 on the board.

Mentions that the series is set up beautifully with the Test match to come as well, but feels that both teams will go hammer and tongs in this match. Informs that Sophie Molineux has a slight niggle and Nicola Carey comes in to replace her.

Knee is fine, says Kaur​​​​​​, India Women's skipper! Harmanpreet Kaur says that as a group, they decided that they want to put a good total on the board. On her injury, Harman mentions that she had a small problem with her left knee, but she is fine now. Informs that they have made two changes with Shafali Verma and Renuka Singh Thakur being rested today, with Amanjot Kaur and Vaishnavi Sharma coming in. Further adds that Vaishnavi is someone who has done brilliantly at the U-19 level and hopes that she can do it on the big stage as well.

Australia Women (Playing XI) - Alyssa Healy (C), Phoebe Litchfield, Georgia Voll, Beth Mooney (WK), Annabel Sutherland, Ashleigh Gardner, Tahlia McGrath, Nicola Carey (replaces Sophie Molineux), Alana King, Megan Schutt, Darcie Brown.

India Women (Playing XI) - Pratika Rawal, Smriti Mandhana, Jemimah Rodrigues, Harmanpreet Kaur (C), Amanjot Kaur (replaces Shafali Verma), Richa Ghosh (WK), Deepti Sharma, Kashvee Gautam, Sree Charani, Kranti Gaud, Vaishnavi Sharma (replaces Renuka Singh Thakur).
TOSS - ​​India Women have won the coin flip and Harmanpreet Kaur, the skipper of India Women, has elected to BAT first.

We are moments away from the all-important coin flip. It will be interesting to see who strides out as the Indian skipper. Will it be Harmanpreet Kaur or Smriti Mandhana? Kaur did injure her knee in the previous game. It is Kaur for India Women and Alyssa Healy for Australia Women.

A tactical outlook - Bellerive Oval usually offers assistance to pace bowlers, particularly under the lights, where the ball is expected to zip and swing significantly. Given the conditions, both teams are likely to lean on pace-heavy attacks. India will rely on the raw talent of Kashvee Gautam and the discipline of Renuka Singh. India Women might also feel the need to bring in Amanjot Kaur, who is one handy all-rounder, but at the cost of whom remains to be seen. Australia Women might just look to give Lucy Hamilton a go alongside Schutt to rattle the Indian top order. With the multi-format series currently locked at 4-4, the winner of this clash takes a pivotal 6-4 lead, placing them in the driver's seat for the remainder of the tour. Stay tuned for toss and team news...

Injury clouds and captaincy dynamics - The fitness of captain Harmanpreet Kaur remains the biggest talking point for the tourists. After suffering a knee injury during her batting stint in the first WODI, she was unable to take the field for the second innings. Kaur's mobility will be closely watched if she decides to take the field. If she is sidelined, Smriti Mandhana will once again take the reins. For Australia Women, Alyssa Healy has done well despite losing a couple of players in the buildup to this ODI series.

India’s quest for clinical execution - India’s primary concern heading into Hobart is consistency both with the bat and in the field. While Smriti Mandhana and Harmanpreet Kaur struck vital half-centuries in the first match, the lack of support from the top order left the team with a sub-par total of 214. The fielding department remains a major headache, as several dropped catches allowed the Aussies to cruise to victory. To keep the series alive, India’s experienced campaigners must step up. Renuka Singh will need to exploit the seam-friendly Hobart conditions early, while the middle order needs a more robust contribution from Jemimah Rodrigues and Deepti Sharma.

Australia’s depth overcomes injury woes - Despite losing stalwarts Ellyse Perry and Kim Garth to quad strains just before the series began, Australia’s legendary bench strength was on full display in the first game. Veteran Megan Schutt returned to the side seamlessly, striking in her first over, while Ashleigh Gardner dismantled the middle order with a three-wicket haul. The batting unit looks equally formidable. Alyssa Healy, playing in her final international home series, is in vintage form. With Beth Mooney anchoring the innings and Annabel Sutherland providing late-order fireworks, the hosts possess a lineup that can adapt to any situation.
